title: The whole step
summary: Two half steps make a whole step: a move that skips exactly one key.

steps.title: Whole step
steps.body:
A **whole step** is two half steps: it skips over exactly one key. C to D is a whole step, with C♯ in between.

**Why it matters:** Most tunes move mainly in half steps and whole steps. Telling the two apart is the first step to hearing how a tune is built.

steps.title: White to black can be a whole step
steps.body:
E to F♯ is a whole step too, even though one key is white and one is black: F sits in between.

**Why it matters:** count the keys, not the colours. A whole step always skips exactly one key.

steps.title: A chain of whole steps
steps.body: C, D, E, F♯: each key is a whole step above the one before it.

steps.title: Half or whole?
steps.body: Play a tune you know and watch the names. For each move, ask yourself whether it was a half step, a whole step or a bigger jump.
